_title: 5 Hotel and Travel Blogs for Arriving by Train and Sleeping Well — WoW Train · glosx.app
_desc: Five independent hotel and travel blogs we trust for choosing where to stay in European cities you can reach by train, from Amsterdam to Rome and Turin.
b1: 5 Hotel and Travel Blogs for Arriving by Train and Sleeping Well
b2: By WoW Train · November 2026 · 6 min read
b3: Arriving by train means arriving in the centre of the city, often a few minutes from your hotel. These five blogs are the ones we read to choose where to stay, and their reviews pair perfectly with a trip by rail.
b4: 1. The Luxury Travel Expert
b5: Careful, detailed hotel reviews with clear opinions. Their guide to the best luxury hotels in Amsterdam is ideal if you arrive on the train from Paris or Brussels.
b6: Read: The best luxury hotels in Amsterdam
b7: 2. A Luxury Travel Blog
b8: One of the longest-running luxury travel blogs, with writers all over the world. A recent post takes you on a high-altitude hike near Innsbruck, a city with direct trains from Vienna and Munich.
b9: Read: A high-altitude hike near Innsbruck
b11: Sharp, up-to-date news from the world’s best hotels. Their piece on the Rome hotel with the city’s most fashionable Christmas tree is a good excuse for a winter train trip to Rome.
b12: Read: Rome's most fashionable Christmas tree
b13: 4. Mrs. O Around The World
b14: Elegant travel with real itineraries. Their five-day Piedmont itinerary through Turin and the Langhe works beautifully with a train arrival in Turin.
b15: Read: 5-day Piedmont itinerary: Turin and the Langhe
b17: Independent city guides covering many European cities, with sections on where to stay, eat and go out. Practical and always local.
b19: Arriving by train? See Paris → Amsterdam, Innsbruck → Vienna, Milan → Rome and Lyon → Turin.
b20: Writing about one of these routes? Take our times with you
b21: Every route page on WoW Train has a block called “Add this route to your blog”: a small card with the route summary and, where we have the official timetable, first train, last train and trains per day. Enter your blog and your name, and you get a short code that shows the card in WordPress, Ghost or any editor, with times that update by themselves. It is free. Try it on Paris → Amsterdam or Tokyo → Kyoto, or find your route in the route index.
b22: Plan the whole route in one go.
b23: Describe your trip and WoW Train suggests the trains for every leg, with booking links.
